# Adjudication Task — Chapter 319

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃319화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“용봉표국의 소국주 주화란이 태을무정검 황보 대협을 뵙습니다.”
  6|
  7|주화란은 절도 있게 포권 지례를 취했다.
  8|
  9|태을무정검 황보엄, 과연 명불허전이다. 단순히 눈빛을 마주하는 것만으로도 가슴이 조여 오고 숨이 막히는 듯했다.
 10|
 11|‘종남제일검(綜南第一劍)…….’
 12|
 13|구파일방과 오대세가. 작금의 천하 무림을 지탱하는 열다섯 개의 기둥.
 14|
 15|눈앞에 있는 상대는 그들 중 하나인 종남파 제일의 고수다. 그 이름에 실린 막중한 무게감이 그녀를 짓눌렀다.
 16|
 17|‘하지만 괜찮아.’
 18|
 19|모두가 입을 모아 어렵다고 말하던 표행을 완수했다.
 20|
 21|이 자리에 태을무정검이 아니라 풍운검군이 나왔어도 당당할 수 있는 이유였다.
 22|
 23|“그래, 의뢰한 물건은 잘 가져왔나?”
 24|
 25|“물론입니다.”
 26|
 27|주화란은 대답과 함께 품 안에서 천년설삼이 든 목곽을 꺼내 들었다. 목곽 전체를 칭칭 동여맨 새끼줄의 매듭에는 작은 글씨가 쓰여 있었다.
 28|
 29|
 30|
 31|산동(山東) 성수장가(性修長家).
 32|
 33|
 34|
 35|글자를 확인한 황보엄이 고개를 끄덕였다.
 36|
 37|“틀림없군. 성수장가의 인(封)이야.”
 38|
 39|사람들은 말한다.
 40|
 41|사천에 당가(唐家)가 있다면, 산동에는 성수장가가 있다고.
 42|
 43|성수장가는 그만큼 의술로 유명한 곳이었다. 무림 세가인 사천당가와 달리 의술에 뿌리를 둔 명망 높은 의가(醫家)이기도 했다.
 44|
 45|종남파는 바로 그 성수장가를 통해 천년설삼을 구입, 용봉표국에 운송을 맡겼다.
 46|
 47|“성수장가의 현 가주이신 환의(丸醫)께서 직접 천년설삼을 넣으시고 서명하셨습니다.”
 48|
 49|“오호, 환의가 직접?”
 50|
 51|“예. 뿐만 아니라 저를 포함한 공증인 여럿이 함께 지켜보았지요.”
 52|
 53|“나이답지 않게 철두철미하군.”
 54|
 55|황보엄의 주름진 손가락이 흰 수염을 쓸어내렸다.
 56|
 57|“군자검의 여식이 뛰어난 재녀(才女)라는 말은 노부도 들어서 알고 있지. 고맙네, 어려운 의뢰를 확실히 처리해 주어서.”
 58|
 59|“저희 용봉표국은 표행에 있어 한 치의 실수도 용납하지 않습니다.”
 60|
 61|“그러니 섬서 제일이라 불리는 것이겠지. 본문도 표국을 운영 중이지만, 역시 용봉표국에 비할 바는 아니야. 허허허.”
 62|
 63|주화란은 가슴이 두근거렸다.
 64|
 65|황보엄의 칭찬에 기뻐서?
 66|
 67|아니었다. 그것과는 무관한, 가슴을 옥죄는 어떤 감정 때문이었다. 그리고 그녀는 그 감정의 이름을 알고 있었다.
 68|
 69|불안감.
 70|
 71|‘뭔가 잘못됐어.’
 72|
 73|그건 예지에 가까운 직감이었다. 그러나 주화란이 불안감의 정체를 더듬어 보기도 전에, 황보엄의 입술이 열렸다.
 74|
 75|“자, 이제 마지막 절차만 남았군.”
 76|
 77|의뢰한 물품을 확인하고, 인수인계를 증명하기 위해 각자의 수결(手決)을 남긴다.
 78|
 79|일다경도 걸리지 않는 간단한 절차 후, 큰 희생을 치른 넉 달간의 표행은 그렇게 마무리될 것이다.
 80|
 81|분명 그럴 터였다.
 82|
 83|‘……아니, 정말 그럴까?’
 84|
 85|지금껏 느껴 본 적 없는 한기가 등줄기를 훑고 올라온다.
 86|
 87|얼어붙은 주화란의 귓가로 황보엄의 목소리가 파고들었다.
 88|
 89|“뭐 하는 겐가? 어서 물건을 확인시켜 주지 않고.”
 90|
 91|주화란은 천천히 고개를 들었다.
 92|
 93|인자하고 부드러운 목소리. 그러나 노인의 새카만 눈동자는 묘한 빛으로 번들거리고 있었다.
 94|
 95|간신히 쥐어짜 낸 음성이 그녀의 붉은 입술 사이로 흘러나왔다.
 96|
 97|“……황보 대협.”
 98|
 99|“목곽을 열게. 그 손으로 직접.”
100|
101|주화란은 깨달았다. 불안감의 정체를, 자신에게는 이제 물러설 곳이 없음을.
102|
103|결국 그녀에게 남은 선택지는 하나뿐이었다.
104|
105|스스슥.
106|
107|가늘게 떨리는 손가락이 매듭을 풀기 시작했다. 주화란이 지난 넉 달 동안 가슴에 품고 있던 목곽이 마치 처음 보는 물건처럼 낯설게 느껴졌다.
108|
109|‘아니, 아니야. 틀림없어. 절대 그럴 리가…….’
110|
111|그리고 다음 순간.
112|
113|달칵.
114|
115|마침내 목곽이 열리고 내부에 담겨 있던 것이 모습을 드러냈다. 청아한 향기, 곧게 뻗은 뿌리와 서리가 낀 새하얀 몸통.
116|
117|그것은 틀림없는 설삼(雪三)이었다. 그러나 그 광경을 본 모두가 호흡을 멈추고 눈을 부릅떴다.
118|
119|그 숨 막히는 정적 속에서 황보엄의 부드러운 목소리가 울렸다.
120|
121|“재미있군.”
122|
123|황보엄이 주름진 손가락을 까딱이자 막강한 공력이 흘러나온다.
124|
125|허공섭물에 의해 두둥실 떠오른 설삼을 바라보며 그가 말을 이었다.
126|
127|“백년설삼(百年雪蔘)이라…… 지금 노부가 기력이 쇠하여 헛것을 보고 있는 것인가?”
128|
129|누구를 향한 물음인지는 분명하다.
130|
131|모두의 시선이 한쪽을 향해 쏠렸다. 경악한 얼굴의 총표두 허준, 없는 사람처럼 삐딱한 자세로 서 있던 송일섬도 마찬가지였다.
132|
133|수십 쌍의 시선 끝에는 창백한 안색으로 눈을 감고 있는 주화란이 있었다.
134|
135|‘끝났어.’
136|
137|목곽 안에 들어 있던 백년설삼을 본 순간, 그녀는 차마 그 광경을 마주하지 못하고 눈을 감아 버렸다.
138|
139|있을 수도 없고 있어서도 안 되는 일이 벌어졌다.
140|
141|‘직접 보고, 갖고 있기까지 했는데.’
142|
143|도대체 어디서부터 어긋난 것일까.
144|
145|지난 시간이 주마등처럼 캄캄한 눈앞을 스쳐 지나갔다.
146|
147|그녀는 이번 표행에 용봉표국의 사활을 걸었다.
148|
149|종남파가 이번 의뢰에 내건 액수는 실로 막대한 거금. 그러나 실패 시 그 열 배에 달하는 위약금을 내야 한다.
150|
151|그리고 지금, 이 양날의 검은 그녀와 용봉표국의 심장에 틀어박혔다.
152|
153|“어찌 된 일인지는 묻지 않겠네. 어떤 기상천외한 사정으로 천년설삼이 백년설삼으로 둔갑했는지는 궁금하지 않으니 말이야. 허나…….”
154|
155|황보엄은 짐짓 안타깝다는 눈빛으로 주화란을 포함한 용봉표국의 사람들을 쓸어 보았다.
156|
157|“이번 일에 대한 배상은 받아야겠지.”
158|
159|“……!”
160|
161|“본문은 이미 천년설삼의 값으로 성수장가에 은자 십만 냥을 지불했네. 그리고 용봉표국이 표행에 성공했을 시, 운송품의 일 할에 해당하는 은자 만 냥을 표비로 지급하기로 했지.”
162|
163|잃어버린 천년설삼의 값어치와 계약 불이행 시 용봉표국이 내야 하는 열 배의 위약금까지.
164|
165|모두 합한다면 은자 이십만 냥이라는 천문학적인 금액이다. 용봉표국이 가진 대부분을 팔아 치워야 충당할 수 있는 액수.
166|
167|그 사실을 깨달은 주화란의 입술에서 피가 흘렀고, 총표두 허준의 얼굴은 시커멓게 물들었다.
168|
169|“화, 황보 대협. 그것은……!”
170|
171|“은자 이십만 냥. 그 어떤 타협도 허락하지 않겠네.”
172|
173|“아, 아아.”
174|
175|주화란을 따라온 표사들이 탄식을 터트렸다.
176|
177|단 한 사람, 송일섬을 제외하고.
178|
179|그는 십 년 가까이 몸담은 표국이 절망적인 위기에 처했음에도 어떤 반응도 보이지 않았다. 단지 입꼬리를 한차례 실룩거렸을 뿐이었다.
180|
181|그 모습을 스치듯 눈에 담은 황보엄이 가득 채운 찻잔을 주화란에게 내밀었다.
182|
183|“한 잔 받게. 마음이 심란할 때에는 따뜻한 차 한 잔만큼 좋은 것이 없거든.”
184|
185|굳게 감겨 있던 주화란의 긴 속눈썹이 흔들렸다. 천천히 눈을 뜬 그녀가 황보엄을 응시했다.
186|
187|“이것이…… 이것이 종남의 방식입니까?”
188|
189|“글쎄, 노부는 자네가 무슨 소리를 하는 건지 모르겠군.”
190|
191|피식 웃은 황보엄이 자신의 찻잔을 기울였다.
192|
193|역시 떫다. 대를 이어 다루를 물려받은 젊은 주인의 솜씨는 아직 서툴렀다.
194|
195|그러나 어째서일까. 지금 황보엄의 입 안에 맴도는 향과 풍취는 방금 전에 비할 바가 아니었다.
196|
197|“아주 좋아. 삼십 년 전, 그때로 돌아간 기분이 들어.”
198|
199|“……!”
200|
201|“왜 그러나. 식기 전에 어서 들지 않고.”
202|
203|주화란은 말없이 입술을 깨물었다.
204|
205|완벽하게 당했다. 만전에 주의를 기울였음에도 당하고야 말았다.
206|
207|아버지인 군자검 주호군을 대신하여 이 년간 표국을 이끌어 온 그녀다. 크고 작은 시행착오와 실패를 겪었지만, 지금만큼 절망적이었던 적은 없었다.
208|
209|‘전처럼 다시 일어설 수 있을까?’
210|
211|넘어질지언정 쓰러지지는 않았다. 그러나 은자 이십만 냥은 용봉표국을 압사(壓死)시킬 수 있는 파괴력을 지녔다.
212|
213|‘위약금은 지불할 수 있겠지.’
214|
215|가능은 하다.
216|
217|용봉표국이 소유한 모든 전답과 부지를 헐값에 팔아 치우고, 봉급을 지급할 수 없는 수백의 쟁자수와 표사, 표두를 떠나보낸다면.
218|
219|그리고 그러한 일련의 과정이 마무리된 후에 용봉표국은 껍데기만 남아 있을 것이다.
220|
221|‘정말 끝인가? 이대로?’
222|
223|황보엄은 그런 주화란을 재미있다는 눈빛으로 응시했다.
224|
225|용봉표국의 소국주가 제법 뛰어나다는 이야기는 익히 들었다.
226|
227|하지만 그에게는 아직 한참 부족한 어리숫보기에 불과했다.
228|
229|‘끌끌. 가여운지고.’
230|
231|황보엄이 내심 웃음을 터트리던 그때였다.
232|
233|“음?”
234|
235|그의 시선이 문득 다루의 문을 향했다. 점차 가까워지는 몇 사람의 기운 때문이었다.
236|
237|‘이건…….’
238|
239|그것은 초절정의 반열에 오른 황보엄조차 쉽게 넘길 수 없을 정도의 기운이었다.
240|
241|구파일방의 장로급에 비견될 만한 커다란 크기의 공력이 서서히 가까워져 오더니, 이내 다루 앞에서 우뚝 멈췄다.
242|
243|‘혹시, 화산파?’
244|
245|황보엄의 예상은 다음 순간 보기 좋게 빗나갔다.
246|
247|끼이익.
248|
249|“어이고, 마침 차 마시고 싶었는데 여기 딱! 다루가 있네.”
250|
251|맨 앞에서 문을 열고 들어오는 장대한 체구의 청년. 진태경을 바라보는 황보엄의 눈동자가 깊게 가라앉았다.
252|
253|
254|
255|* * *
256|
257|
258|
259|척 보기에도 심상치 않은 광경이다.
260|
261|곳곳에 늘어선 수십여 명의 검객들과 무겁게 가라앉은 공기.
262|
263|‘주화란, 아니 용봉표국은?’
264|
265|의문이 떠오름과 동시에 발견할 수 있었다. 사람들이 에워싸고 있는 어느 탁자 위. 잘게 떨리고 있는 가느다란 손가락을.
266|
267|단 한 번 마주쳤을 뿐이지만 손가락만 봐도 누구인지 알 수 있었다. 거 참, 신기한 일이다.
268|
269|‘음, 손이 예뻤었나.’
270|
271|뒤통수를 긁적이는 내게 사람들의 시선이 날아와 꽂혔다.
272|
273|다루의 주인으로 보이는 중년인 하나가 후다닥 달려와 허리를 굽실거린다.
274|
275|“손님, 죄송하지만 지금은 자리가 꽉 차서…….”
276|
277|“저기 자리 있는데?”
278|
279|“안 쓰는 자립니다.”
280|
281|“그럼 서서 먹지 뭐.”
282|
283|그때, 종남파의 제자로 보이는 무인 하나가 절도 있는 걸음으로 다가와 말했다.
284|
285|“무인이오?”
286|
287|“아뇨. 뚱인데요.”
288|
289|무인이 별 미친놈 보겠다는 눈빛으로 나를 위아래로 훑었다.

[P89]
Ju Hwaran’s long, tightly shut eyelashes trembled. Slowly, she opened her eyes and stared at Hwangbo Eom.

[P90]
“Is this… Is this Zhongnan’s way?”

[P91]
“I’m afraid I don’t know what you mean.”

[P92]
Hwangbo Eom laughed softly and raised his own teacup to his lips.

[P93]
As expected, the tea was astringent. The young owner who had inherited the teahouse from his family was still inexperienced.

[P94]
And yet, for some reason, the aroma and flavor lingering in Hwangbo Eom’s mouth now were incomparable to what he had tasted a moment ago.

[P95]
“Very good. I feel as though I’ve gone back thirty years.”

[P96]
“……!”

[P97]
“What’s wrong? Drink before it gets cold.”

[P98]
Ju Hwaran silently bit her lip.

[P99]
She had been completely outmaneuvered. Despite taking every possible precaution, she had still fallen into their trap.

[P100]
For the past two years, she had led the Escort Bureau in place of her father, the Junzi Sword, Ju Hogun. She had endured all kinds of mistakes and failures, both large and small, but never had she faced anything as hopeless as this.

[P101]
*Can I rise again like before?*

[P102]
She had stumbled before, but she had never stayed down. Yet two hundred thousand silver nyang was enough to crush the Yongbong Escort Bureau out of existence.

[P103]
*We can pay the penalty.*

[P104]
It was possible.

[P105]
They would have to sell every field and parcel of land owned by the Yongbong Escort Bureau for a pittance, then send away the hundreds of caravan porters, escorts, and Escort Captains whose wages they could no longer afford.

[P106]
And once that entire process was over, nothing would remain of the Yongbong Escort Bureau but an empty shell.

[P107]
*Is it really over? Just like this?*

[P108]
Hwangbo Eom watched Ju Hwaran with amusement.

[P109]
He had long heard that the Young Bureau Head of the Yongbong Escort Bureau was quite capable.

[P110]
But to him, she was still nothing more than a naive greenhorn.

[P111]
*Heh. How pitiful.*

[P112]
Just as Hwangbo Eom chuckled inwardly—

[P113]
“Hmm?”

[P114]
His gaze suddenly turned toward the teahouse door. The presence of several people was drawing closer.

[P115]
*This is…*

[P116]
Among them was an aura so powerful that even Hwangbo Eom, a Supreme Peak master, could not easily dismiss it.

[P117]
A vast reserve of internal energy comparable to that of an Elder from the Nine Sects and One Gang steadily approached, then stopped directly outside the teahouse.

[P118]
*Could it be Huashan?*

[P119]
Hwangbo Eom’s prediction was proven spectacularly wrong the next moment.

[P120]
*Creaaak.*

[P121]
“Oh, I was just in the mood for some tea, and look at that! A teahouse, right when I needed one.”

[P122]
A broad-shouldered young man opened the door and strode in at the head of the group.

[P123]
Hwangbo Eom’s eyes darkened as he looked at Jin Taekyung.

[P124]
* * *

[P125]
Even at a glance, something was clearly wrong.

[P126]
Dozens of swordsmen stood throughout the room, and the air hung heavy.

[P127]
*Ju Hwaran—or rather, the Yongbong Escort Bureau?*

[P128]
The question had barely crossed my mind when I spotted them.

[P129]
On top of a table surrounded by people, slender fingers trembled faintly.

[P130]
I had only met her once, but I could tell who she was just from her fingers. Funny how that worked.

[P131]
*Were her hands pretty?*

[P132]
As I scratched the back of my head, everyone’s gaze flew toward me.

[P133]
A middle-aged man who appeared to be the owner of the teahouse hurried over, bowing repeatedly.

[P134]
“Sir, I’m sorry, but we’re completely full right now…”

[P135]
“There’s a seat over there.”

[P136]
“That seat isn’t in use.”

[P137]
“Then I’ll drink standing up.”

[P138]
At that moment, a martial artist who appeared to be a Disciple of the Zhongnan Sect approached with measured steps.

[P139]
“Are you a martial artist?”

[P140]
“No, I’m fat.”

[P141]

[P142]
“I don’t know who you are or where you come from, but an important person is here. You would do well to leave.”

[P143]
“I’m an important son in my family too, so why should I? There’s plenty of room anyway.”

[P144]
“……You’re being troublesome. I am a Disciple of the Great Zhongnan Sect. I’m sure you understand now, so leave.”

[P145]
“Why do you keep ordering me around? I just want to sit down and have some tea.”

[P146]
Cheongpung, who had been fidgeting behind me, shouted excitedly.

[P147]
“Benefactor! Candied sweets too!”

[P148]
“Candied sweets? Hey, Mujin. Does this teahouse sell those too?”

[P149]
“Are you seriously asking that right now?”

[P150]
*What the hell is wrong with these guys?*

[P151]
The Zhongnan Sect disciple had been looking at us as if he were thinking exactly that, but his face stiffened when he spotted someone.

[P152]
“H-Huashan’s Lone Crane, Baek Museong!”

[P153]
Maybe it was because this was Huashan’s home ground, but quite a few people here recognized Baek Museong.

[P154]
In any case, the Zhongnan Disciple’s involuntary shout had an immediate effect. Unlike when we first entered, everyone was looking at us now.

[P155]
Two gazes stood out from the rest.

[P156]
I waved at one of them.

[P157]
“Oh, we meet again.”

[P158]
“…Young Hero Jin?”

[P159]
Ju Hwaran stared at me, her pale face framed by wide, round eyes.

[P160]
Across from her sat an old man with a long white beard.

[P161]
I gave Ju Hwaran a small smile, then gazed at the old man.

[P162]
“Is there some problem between you and Young Lady Ju?”

[P163]
The old man—the Taeeul Merciless Sword, Hwangbo Eom—stroked his beard and laughed.

[P164]
“An interesting fellow has appeared.”

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

[P66]
Something that could not and should not have happened had happened.

[P67]

[P68]
Where had everything gone wrong?

[P69]
The time that had passed flashed before her eyes in the darkness.

[P70]

[P74]

“We will have to receive compensation for this matter.”

“……!”

The value of the lost Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng, plus the tenfold penalty the Yongbong Escort Bureau owed for failing to fulfill the contract.

[P80]

“G-Great Hero Hwangbo, that is…!”

[P82]

[P83]
“A-Ah…”

[P85]

[P86]

[P87]

[P88]

[P89]

[P90]
“Is this… Is this Zhongnan’s way?”

[P91]
“I’m afraid I don’t know what you mean.”

[P92]

[P93]

[P94]

[P95]
“Very good. I feel as though I’ve gone back thirty years.”

[P96]
“……!”

[P97]
“What’s wrong? Drink before it gets cold.”

[P100]

*We can pay the penalty.*

[P105]

*Is it really over? Just like this?*

*Heh. How pitiful.*

“Hmm?”

[P115]
*This is…*

[P117]

[P118]
*Could it be Huashan?*

[P119]

[P120]
*Creaaak.*

[P121]

[P122]

[P123]
Hwangbo Eom’s eyes darkened as he looked at Jin Taekyung.

[P124]
* * *

[P125]

[P126]

[P127]
*Ju Hwaran—or rather, the Yongbong Escort Bureau?*

[P128]

[P129]
On top of a table surrounded by people, slender fingers trembled faintly.

[P130]

[P131]
*Were her hands pretty?*

[P132]

[P133]

[P134]
“Sir, I’m sorry, but we’re completely full right now…”

[P135]
“There’s a seat over there.”

[P136]
“That seat isn’t in use.”

[P137]
“Then I’ll drink standing up.”

[P138]

[P139]
“Are you a martial artist?”

[P140]
“No, I’m fat.”

[P141]

[P142]

[P143]
“I’m an important son in my family too, so why should I? There’s plenty of room anyway.”

[P144]
“……You’re being troublesome. I am a Disciple of the Great Zhongnan Sect. I’m sure you understand now, so leave.”

[P145]
“Why do you keep ordering me around? I just want to sit down and have some tea.”

[P146]
Cheongpung, who had been fidgeting behind me, shouted excitedly.

[P147]
“Benefactor! Candied sweets too!”

[P148]
“Candied sweets? Hey, Mujin. Does this teahouse sell those too?”

[P149]
“Are you seriously asking that right now?”

[P150]
*What the hell is wrong with these guys?*

[P151]
The Zhongnan Sect disciple had been looking at us as if he were thinking exactly that, but his face stiffened when he spotted someone.

[P152]
“H-Huashan’s Lone Crane, Baek Museong!”

[P153]
Maybe it was because this was Huashan’s home ground, but quite a few people here recognized Baek Museong.

[P154]
In any case, the Zhongnan Disciple’s involuntary shout had an immediate effect. Unlike when we first entered, everyone was looking at us now.

[P155]
Two gazes stood out from the rest.

[P156]
I waved at one of them.

[P157]
“Oh, we meet again.”

[P158]
“…Young Hero Jin?”

[P159]
Ju Hwaran stared at me, her pale face framed by wide, round eyes.

[P160]
Across from her sat an old man with a long white beard.

[P161]
I gave Ju Hwaran a small smile, then gazed at the old man.

[P162]
“Is there some problem between you and Young Lady Ju?”

[P163]

[P164]
“An interesting fellow has appeared.”

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.

- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.

- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
